# The Python API of tlrender: generated from the bindings by nanobind's
# stubgen, with each description taken from the C++ headers. Do not edit:
# see docs/pythonstubs.py. Import it as "import tlrender".

"""
tlRender is an open source library for building playback and review applications for visual effects, film, and animation.

Start with init(context), then:

- Timeline: a timeline, movie or image sequence opened for playback, from a file or an opentimelineio Timeline object. getVideo(time) returns a decoded frame, for a script that wants frames rather than playback.
- Player: plays a Timeline; currentVideo has its decoded frames, one per timeline when comparing. Nothing updates without Context.tick(), which does not wait for decoding: sleep a little between calls.
- OffscreenRender: draws those frames to an image without a window, a tile or wipe compare included -- headless on Linux with SDL_VIDEO_DRIVER=offscreen.
- WriteSystem: writes images and movies.

An image's pixels are numpy.asarray(image), row zero at the top. The ui module has the widgets: Viewport, TimelineWidget and the rest.
"""

from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping, Sequence
import datetime
import enum
from typing import overload

import feather_tk._feather_tk
import opentimelineio.opentime

from tlrender._tlrender import ui as ui

VERSION_DEV: str = '-dev'

VERSION_FULL: str = '0.29.0-dev'

class AudioInfo:
    """Audio data information."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """Audio name."""

    @name.setter
    def name(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def channelCount(self) -> int:
        """Number of channels."""

    @channelCount.setter
    def channelCount(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def type(self) -> AudioType:
        """Sample data type."""

    @type.setter
    def type(self, arg: AudioType, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def sampleRate(self) -> int:
        """Sample rate in hertz."""

    @sampleRate.setter
    def sampleRate(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def isValid(self) -> bool:
        """Is the audio valid?"""

    @property
    def byteCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the byte count."""

    def __eq__(self, arg: AudioInfo, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: AudioInfo, /) -> bool: ...

class Audio:
    """Audio data."""
    def __init__(self, info: AudioInfo, sampleCount: int) -> None:
        """Create new audio."""

    @property
    def info(self) -> AudioInfo:
        """Get the audio information."""

    @property
    def channelCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the audio channel count."""

    @property
    def type(self) -> AudioType:
        """Get the audio data type."""

    @property
    def sampleRate(self) -> int:
        """Get the audio sample rate."""

    @property
    def sampleCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the audio sample count."""

    @property
    def isValid(self) -> bool:
        """Is the audio valid?"""

    @property
    def byteCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the audio data byte count."""

    def zero(self) -> None:
        """Zero the audio data."""

class AudioResample:
    """Resample audio data."""
    def __init__(self, input: AudioInfo, output: AudioInfo) -> None:
        """Create a new resampler."""

    @property
    def inputInfo(self) -> AudioInfo:
        """Get the input audio information."""

    @property
    def outputInfo(self) -> AudioInfo:
        """Get the output audio information."""

    def process(self, audio: Audio) -> Audio:
        """Resample audio data.

        Resample audio data into a buffer with room for
        getOutputSampleCountMax() samples, and return how many were written.
        Nothing is allocated, which is what the audio thread needs.
        """

    def flush(self) -> None:
        """Flush any remaining data."""

class FileType(enum.IntFlag):
    """File types. The values are a bit mask; getExts() takes a combination of
    them.
    """
    __str__ = __repr__

    def __repr__(self, /):
        """Return repr(self)."""

    Unknown = 0

    Media = 1

    Seq = 2

    Audio = 4

class IOInfo:
    """I/O information."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def video(self) -> list[feather_tk._feather_tk.ImageInfo]:
        """Video layer information."""

    @video.setter
    def video(self, arg: Sequence[feather_tk._feather_tk.ImageInfo], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def videoTime(self) -> opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange | None:
        """Video time range, unset when there is no video."""

    @videoTime.setter
    def videoTime(self, arg: opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange | None, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def audio(self) -> AudioInfo:
        """Audio information."""

    @audio.setter
    def audio(self, arg: AudioInfo, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def audioTime(self) -> opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange | None:
        """Audio time range, unset when there is no audio."""

    @audioTime.setter
    def audioTime(self, arg: opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange | None, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def tags(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Metadata tags read from the file. Only what the file itself carries:
        the information describing the video and the audio is above, not mixed
        in here.
        """

    @tags.setter
    def tags(self, arg: Mapping[str, str], /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: IOInfo, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: IOInfo, /) -> bool: ...

class IIO:
    """Base class for readers and writers."""
    @property
    def path(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Path:
        """Get the path."""

    @staticmethod
    def getObjectCount() -> int:
        """Get the number of objects currenty instantiated."""

class IIOPlugin:
    """Base class for I/O plugins."""
    @property
    def pluginName(self) -> str:
        """Get the plugin name."""

    def getPluginInfo(self, options: Mapping[str, str] = {}) -> str:
        """Get the plugin information."""

    def getExts(self, types: int = 7) -> set[str]:
        """Get the supported file extensions."""

class MissingFrames(enum.Enum):
    """What to do about a frame a sequence does not have.

    The first three match OTIO's image sequence reference policies, which is
    where the value comes from when the sequence is described by a timeline.
    They are decided per read: the sequence keeps its length and each of them
    says what fills a gap.

    The last two are different in kind. They do not fill anything; they say
    what the timeline is built out of, so a clip covers each run of frames that
    are there and no read ever asks for a frame that is not. That makes them
    structural: they are settled when the sequence is opened, and changing one
    means opening it again. Because the frames are found in order to build the
    clips, they only apply to an image sequence opened directly -- a timeline
    that was authored already says what its clips are, and those are not ours
    to rewrite.
    """
    Error = 0
    """The frame does not read."""

    Hold = 1
    """Repeat the nearest frame before it."""

    Black = 2
    """A blank frame."""

    Skip = 3
    """Leave it out; only the frames that are there play."""

    Gaps = 4
    """Leave a hole, so the frames keep the times they had."""

def getMissingFramesEnums() -> list[MissingFrames]:
    """Get every value of MissingFrames."""

def isStructural(missingFrames: MissingFrames) -> bool:
    """Get whether a policy is settled when the sequence is opened, by deciding
    the clips, rather than per read.
    """

class SeqOptions:
    """Sequence I/O options.

    The default speed is the rate of a sequence whose files do not say what
    theirs is. The options can also give "SeqIO/Speed", the rate when something
    more specific than the files says what it is, such as a timeline's image
    sequence reference. That one is used whatever the files say.
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def defaultSpeed(self) -> float:
        """Frame rate, in frames per second, of a sequence whose files do not
        give one.
        """

    @defaultSpeed.setter
    def defaultSpeed(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def missingFrames(self) -> MissingFrames:
        """What to do about a frame the sequence does not have."""

    @missingFrames.setter
    def missingFrames(self, arg: MissingFrames, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: SeqOptions, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: SeqOptions, /) -> bool: ...

class IRead(IIO):
    """Base class for readers.

    A reader is stateful -- a movie carries a demuxer position -- which is what
    separates it from a decoder. What it reads is video or audio, one of the
    two classes below: they share nothing but the file, and plenty of files
    have only one of them.
    """
    def cancelRequests(self) -> None:
        """Cancel pending requests."""

    @property
    def error(self) -> str:
        """Get the first error encountered while reading, or an empty string.
        Errors are also sent to the log. The default implementation returns an
        empty string.
        """

    @property
    def errorCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of errors encountered while reading. The default
        implementation returns zero.
        """

class IVideoRead(IRead):
    """Base class for video readers."""
    pass

class IAudioRead(IRead):
    """Base class for audio readers."""
    pass

class IReadPlugin(IIOPlugin):
    """Base class for read plugins."""
    def videoRead(self, path: feather_tk._feather_tk.Path, options: Mapping[str, str] = {}) -> IVideoRead:
        """Create a video reader for the given path, or null when this format
        has no video, or is decoded rather than read: a sequence of stateless
        files needs no reader, and decode() returns one for it instead.

        Create a video reader for the given path and memory locations.
        """

    def audioRead(self, path: feather_tk._feather_tk.Path, options: Mapping[str, str] = {}) -> IAudioRead:
        """Create an audio reader for the given path, or null when this format
        has no audio.

        Create an audio reader for the given path and memory locations.
        """

class IWrite(IIO):
    """Base class for writers."""
    def writeVideo(self, time: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime, image: feather_tk._feather_tk.Image, options: Mapping[str, str] = {}) -> None:
        """Write video data."""

    def writeAudio(self, timeRange: opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange, audio: Audio, options: Mapping[str, str] = {}) -> None:
        """Write audio data. The default implementation does nothing; writers
        that support audio should override this. Audio is expected to be
        written sequentially, starting at the beginning of the audio time range
        given in the IOInfo.
        """

    def finish(self) -> None:
        """Finish writing, flushing any buffered data and finalizing the file.
        This is called automatically by the destructor, but since destructors
        cannot throw, errors that occur while finalizing are only logged. Call
        finish() explicitly to have those errors reported as exceptions.
        """

class IWritePlugin(IIOPlugin):
    """Base class for write plugins."""
    def getInfo(self, info: feather_tk._feather_tk.ImageInfo, options: Mapping[str, str] = {}) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.ImageInfo:
        """Get information for writing."""

    def write(self, path: feather_tk._feather_tk.Path, info: IOInfo, options: Mapping[str, str] = {}) -> IWrite:
        """Create a writer for the given path."""

class ReadSystem(feather_tk._feather_tk.ISystem):
    """Read system."""
    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context) -> None:
        """Create a new system."""

    @property
    def plugins(self) -> list[IReadPlugin]:
        """Get the list of plugins."""

    def addPlugin(self, plugin: IReadPlugin) -> None:
        """Add a plugin."""

    def removePlugin(self, plugin: IReadPlugin) -> None:
        """Remove a plugin."""

    def getPlugin(self, path: feather_tk._feather_tk.Path) -> IReadPlugin:
        """Get a plugin.

        Get a plugin for the given path.
        """

    @property
    def names(self) -> list[str]:
        """Get the plugin names."""

    def getExts(self, types: int = 3) -> set[str]:
        """Get the supported file extensions."""

    def getFileType(self, extension: str) -> FileType:
        """Get the file type for the given extension."""

    def videoRead(self, path: feather_tk._feather_tk.Path, options: Mapping[str, str] = {}) -> IVideoRead:
        """Create a video reader for the given path, or null when the format
        has no video or is decoded rather than read.

        Create a video reader for the given path and memory locations.
        """

    def audioRead(self, path: feather_tk._feather_tk.Path, options: Mapping[str, str] = {}) -> IAudioRead:
        """Create an audio reader for the given path, or null when the format
        has no audio.

        Create an audio reader for the given path and memory locations.
        """

class WriteSystem(feather_tk._feather_tk.ISystem):

    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context) -> None:

        """Remove a plugin."""

    def getPlugin(self, path: feather_tk._feather_tk.Path) -> IWritePlugin:
        """Get a plugin.

        Get a plugin for the given path.
        """

    @property
    def names(self) -> list[str]:
        """Get the plugin names."""

    def getExts(self, types: int = 3) -> set[str]:
        """Get the supported file extensions."""

    def getFileType(self, extension: str) -> FileType:
        """Get the file type for the given extension."""

    def write(self, path: feather_tk._feather_tk.Path, info: IOInfo, options: Mapping[str, str] = {}) -> IWrite:
        """Create a writer for the given path."""

def init(context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context) -> None:
    """
    Initialize the library: the I/O, audio and render systems, added to the context. Once, before making timelines or players. Without a display or sound card -- a container, a render farm -- set SDL_AUDIO_DRIVER=dummy in the environment first: audio then goes nowhere, and the system's audio libraries are not asked for devices, which is what prints their errors when there are none.
    """

class AudioLayer:
    """Audio layer."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def audio(self) -> Audio:
        """Audio data: one second of it, silent where the clip does not cover
        the second.
        """

    @audio.setter
    def audio(self, arg: Audio, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: AudioLayer, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: AudioLayer, /) -> bool: ...

class AudioFrame:
    """Audio frame."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def seconds(self) -> float:
        """Time the frame starts at, in seconds. A frame is one second of
        audio.
        """

    @seconds.setter
    def seconds(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def layers(self) -> list[AudioLayer]:
        """One layer for each audio clip under the frame's second, or one
        silent layer when there are none.
        """

    @layers.setter
    def layers(self, arg: Sequence[AudioLayer], /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: AudioFrame, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: AudioFrame, /) -> bool: ...

class AudioFrameListObserver:
    """List observer."""
    def __init__(self, observableList: IObservableAudioFrameList, callback: Callable[[Sequence[AudioFrame]], None], action: feather_tk._feather_tk.ObserverAction = feather_tk._feather_tk.ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class IObservableAudioFrameList:
    """Base class for observable lists."""
    pass

class ObservableAudioFrameList(IObservableAudioFrameList):
    """Observable list."""
    def __init__(self, arg: Sequence[AudioFrame], /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: Sequence[AudioFrame], /) -> None:
        """Set the list."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: Sequence[AudioFrame], /) -> bool:
        """Set the list only if it has changed."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear the list."""

    def setItem(self, index: int, value: AudioFrame) -> None:
        """Set an item."""

    def setItemOnlyIfChanged(self, index: int, value: AudioFrame) -> bool:
        """Set an item only if it has changed."""

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: AudioFrame, /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: Sequence[AudioFrame], /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    def insertItem(self, index: int, value: AudioFrame) -> None:
        """Insert an item."""

    def insertItems(self, index: int, list: Sequence[AudioFrame]) -> None:
        """Insert a range of items."""

    def removeItem(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Remove an item."""

    def removeItems(self, start: int, end: int) -> None:
        """Remove a range of items."""

    def replaceItems(self, start: int, end: int, list: Sequence[AudioFrame]) -> None:
        """Replace a range of items."""

    def get(self) -> list[AudioFrame]:
        """Get the list."""

    def getSize(self) -> int:
        """Get the list size."""

    def isEmpty(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the list is empty."""

    def getItem(self, arg: int, /) -> AudioFrame:
        """Get a list item."""

    def contains(self, arg: AudioFrame, /) -> bool:
        """Does the list contain the given item?"""

    def indexOf(self, arg: AudioFrame, /) -> int:
        """Get the index of the given item."""

@overload
def isTimeEqual(arg0: AudioFrame, arg1: AudioFrame, /) -> bool:
    """Compare the time values of audio frames.

    Compare the time values of video frames.
    """

@overload
def isTimeEqual(arg0: VideoFrame, arg1: VideoFrame, /) -> bool:
    """Compare the time values of audio frames.

    Compare the time values of video frames.
    """

class AudioDeviceID:

    @property

class AudioSystem(feather_tk._feather_tk.ISystem):
    """Audio system."""
    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context) -> None:
        """Create a new system."""

    @property
    def drivers(self) -> list[str]:
        """Get the list of audio drivers."""

    @property
    def currentDriver(self) -> str:
        """Get the current audio driver."""

    @property
    def bufferFrameCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the size of the buffer the audio device is asked for, in sample
        frames. Zero is the device's own default.
        """

    @bufferFrameCount.setter
    def bufferFrameCount(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def devices(self) -> list[AudioDeviceInfo]:
        """Get the list of audio devices."""

    @property
    def observeDevices(self) -> IObservableAudioDeviceInfoList:
        """Observe the list of audio devices."""

    @property
    def defaultDevice(self) -> AudioDeviceInfo:
        """Get the default audio device."""

    @property
    def observeDefaultDevice(self) -> IObservableAudioDeviceInfo:
        """Observe the default audio device."""

class Background(enum.Enum):
    """Background type."""
    Solid = 0

    Checkers = 1

    Gradient = 2

def getBackgroundEnums() -> list[Background]:
    """Get every value of Background."""

class Outline:
    """Outline."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        """Whether an outline is drawn around each image shown."""

    @enabled.setter
    def enabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def width(self) -> int:
        """The outline width, in view pixels, outside the image's edge."""

    @width.setter
    def width(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def color(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F:
        """The outline color."""

    @color.setter
    def color(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: Outline, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: Outline, /) -> bool: ...

class BackgroundOptions:
    """Background options."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def type(self) -> Background:
        """The background type."""

    @type.setter
    def type(self, arg: Background, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def solidColor(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F:
        """The color for Background::Solid."""

    @solidColor.setter
    def solidColor(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def checkersColor(self) -> tuple[feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F, feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F]:
        """The two checker colors, for Background::Checkers."""

    @checkersColor.setter
    def checkersColor(self, arg: tuple[feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F, feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def checkersSize(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Size2I:
        """The size of each checker, in view pixels."""

    @checkersSize.setter
    def checkersSize(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.Size2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def gradientColor(self) -> tuple[feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F, feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F]:
        """The top and bottom colors, for Background::Gradient."""

    @gradientColor.setter
    def gradientColor(self, arg: tuple[feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F, feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def outline(self) -> Outline:
        """The outline around the images."""

    @outline.setter
    def outline(self, arg: Outline, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: BackgroundOptions, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: BackgroundOptions, /) -> bool: ...

        """Get the value."""

@overload
def to_json(arg: Background, /) -> str:
    """Serialize a path.

    The frames a path covers are its own state rather than part of its name, so
    a path written as its name alone comes back naming one file. This writes
    them beside it, as data: a sequence has a run for each hole in it, with a
    step as well as a range, and a name made to carry all of that would have to
    be parsed back out again.

    A path whose name already says what it covers -- a single file, or one
    frame -- is written as that name, so the ordinary case reads and writes as
    it always did.
    """

@overload

def from_json(arg0: str, arg1: DisplayOptions, /) -> None:
    """Convert from JSON, given as a string, into the given value."""

def from_json(arg0: str, arg1: Grid, /) -> None:

class OCIOConfig(enum.Enum):
    """OpenColorIO configuration options."""
    BuiltIn = 0
    """The configuration built into OpenColorIO, "ocio://default"."""

    EnvironmentVariable = 1

    File = 2
    """The configuration file in OCIOOptions::fileName."""

def getOCIOConfigEnums() -> list[OCIOConfig]:
    """Get every value of OCIOConfig."""

class OCIOOptions:
    """OpenColorIO options."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        """Whether OpenColorIO color management is applied. It takes effect
        only with a display, a view, and an input color space (this one's or
        DisplayOptions::ocioInput).
        """

    @enabled.setter
    def enabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def config(self) -> OCIOConfig:
        """Where the configuration comes from."""

    @config.setter
    def config(self, arg: OCIOConfig, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def fileName(self) -> str:
        """The configuration file, for OCIOConfig::File."""

    @fileName.setter
    def fileName(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def input(self) -> str:
        """The input color space, by name in the configuration."""

    @input.setter
    def input(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def display(self) -> str:
        """The display, by name in the configuration."""

    @display.setter
    def display(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def view(self) -> str:
        """The view, by name in the configuration."""

    @view.setter
    def view(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def look(self) -> str:
        """The look, by name in the configuration; empty for none."""

    @look.setter
    def look(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: OCIOOptions, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: OCIOOptions, /) -> bool: ...

class LUTDirection(enum.Enum):
    """LUT direction.

    Forward is the direction the file itself reads. An ICC monitor profile
    reads from the monitor's code values, so correcting the display with one
    takes Inverse.
    """
    Forward = 0

    Inverse = 1

def getLUTDirectionEnums() -> list[LUTDirection]:
    """Get every value of LUTDirection."""

class LUTOrder(enum.Enum):
    """LUT operation order."""
    PostConfig = 0
    """Applied after the color adjustments and the OpenColorIO display
    transform.
    """

    PreConfig = 1
    """Applied before the OpenColorIO input conversion and the color
    adjustments.
    """

def getLUTOrderEnums() -> list[LUTOrder]:
    """Get every value of LUTOrder."""

    @fileName.setter

    @property
    def direction(self) -> LUTDirection:
        """The direction the LUT is applied in."""

    @direction.setter
    def direction(self, arg: LUTDirection, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def order(self) -> LUTOrder:

    @order.setter
    def order(self, arg: LUTOrder, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: LUTOptions, /) -> bool: ...

class Compare(enum.Enum):
    """Comparison modes."""
    B = 1

    Wipe = 2

    Butterfly = 3
    """The same half of each file, one of them mirrored, so that the two meet
    at the middle on the same picture. What a side by side comparison cannot do
    is put the same thing next to itself, which is what judging a colour
    adjustment needs.
    """

    Overlay = 4

    Difference = 5

    Horizontal = 6

    Vertical = 7

    Tile = 8

def getCompareEnums() -> list[Compare]:
    """Get every value of Compare."""

class CompareTime(enum.Enum):
    """Comparison time modes."""
    Relative = 0
    """Each file at the same offset from the start of its time range."""

    Absolute = 1
    """Each file at the same time, whatever its time range."""

def getCompareTimeEnums() -> list[CompareTime]:
    """Get every value of CompareTime."""

def getCompareTime(sourceTime: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime, sourceTimeRange: opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange, compareTimeRange: opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange, compareTime: CompareTime = CompareTime.Relative) -> opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime:
    """
    The time in a compared timeline for a time in this one, as a Player finds it: Relative counts from each timeline's start, in the compared one's rate, Absolute takes the time as it is. For Timeline.getVideo() on the compared timeline.
    """

class CompareOptions:
    """
    How compared timelines are drawn together: compare is the mode (None for this timeline alone, B, Wipe, Butterfly, Overlay, Difference, Horizontal, Vertical, Tile), and the other fields are the settings for the modes that have them. Read by whatever draws the frames, a viewport or a renderer; which frames there are is the Player's compare.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def compare(self) -> Compare:
        """The comparison mode."""

    @compare.setter
    def compare(self, arg: Compare, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def wipeCenter(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.V2F:
        """The wipe center, as a fraction of the first image's width and
        height; (0, 0) is the top left.
        """

    @wipeCenter.setter
    def wipeCenter(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.V2F, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def wipeRotation(self) -> float:
        """The wipe rotation, in degrees. At zero the wipe line is vertical,
        with A on the left and B on the right.
        """

    @wipeRotation.setter
    def wipeRotation(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def overlay(self) -> float:
        """The opacity of A over B in the overlay comparison, from 0 to 1."""

    @overlay.setter
    def overlay(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def differenceGain(self) -> float:
        """What the difference is multiplied by before it is shown. The
        differences worth looking for are often a code value or two -- what a
        compressed version differs from its source by -- and at their own size
        they are indistinguishable from black.
        """

    @differenceGain.setter
    def differenceGain(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def sameSize(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the other files are sized to the first: fitted to its box
        where they are drawn over it, as tall as it side by side, as wide as it
        one above the other, and fitted to tiles its size. Otherwise each keeps
        its own size, and the tiles are as large as the largest file.
        """

    @sameSize.setter
    def sameSize(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: CompareOptions, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: CompareOptions, /) -> bool: ...

class CompareOptionsObserver:
    """Value observer."""
    def __init__(self, observable: IObservableCompareOptions, callback: Callable[[CompareOptions], None], action: feather_tk._feather_tk.ObserverAction = feather_tk._feather_tk.ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class Color:
    """Color values."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the color values are applied."""

    @enabled.setter
    def enabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def add(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.V3F:
        """Added to the red, green, and blue before the other values are
        applied; zero does nothing.
        """

    @add.setter
    def add(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.V3F, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def brightness(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.V3F:
        """Brightness, a multiplier for each channel; one does nothing."""

    @brightness.setter
    def brightness(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.V3F, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def contrast(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.V3F:
        """Contrast for each channel, pivoting on 0.5; one does nothing."""

    @contrast.setter
    def contrast(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.V3F, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def saturation(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.V3F:
        """Saturation for each channel; one does nothing and zero is gray."""

    @saturation.setter
    def saturation(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.V3F, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def hue(self) -> float:
        """Hue rotation in turns: 0.5 is half way round the color wheel, and
        zero does nothing.
        """

    @hue.setter
    def hue(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: Color, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: Color, /) -> bool: ...

def color(arg: Color, /) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.M44F:
    """Marker color; see getMarkerColor()."""

class Levels:
    """Levels values."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the levels are applied."""

    @enabled.setter
    def enabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def inLow(self) -> float:
        """The input black point: the value that becomes outLow."""

    @inLow.setter
    def inLow(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def inHigh(self) -> float:
        """The input white point: the value that becomes outHigh. Values
        outside the input range are not clamped.
        """

    @inHigh.setter
    def inHigh(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def gamma(self) -> float:
        """The gamma: after the input range, each value that is not negative is
        raised to one over it, so above one brightens the midtones.
        """

    @gamma.setter
    def gamma(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def outLow(self) -> float:
        """The output black point."""

    @outLow.setter
    def outLow(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def outHigh(self) -> float:
        """The output white point."""

    @outHigh.setter
    def outHigh(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: Levels, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: Levels, /) -> bool: ...

class Exposure:
    """A plain stop adjustment: the value scales the image by 2^stops, so zero
    is neutral. The old exrdisplay-style defog, knee, and gamma are gone --
    SoftClip and Levels cover them, and the exrdisplay formula was never
    neutral at its defaults.
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the exposure is applied."""

    @enabled.setter
    def enabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def exposure(self) -> float:
        """The exposure, in stops."""

    @exposure.setter
    def exposure(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: Exposure, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: Exposure, /) -> bool: ...

class SoftClip:
    """Soft clip."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the soft clip is applied."""

    @enabled.setter
    def enabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> float:
        """The amount, from 0 to 1: values above one minus the amount are
        rolled off toward one rather than passing it. Zero does nothing.
        """

    @value.setter
    def value(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: SoftClip, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: SoftClip, /) -> bool: ...

class AspectRatio:
    """Aspect ratio."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, num: float, den: float = 1.0) -> None: ...

    @property
    def num(self) -> float:
        """The numerator, the width part of the ratio."""

    @num.setter
    def num(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def den(self) -> float:
        """The denominator, the height part of the ratio."""

    @den.setter
    def den(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def isValid(self) -> bool:
        """Whether both parts are positive."""

    def __float__(self) -> float: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: AspectRatio, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: AspectRatio, /) -> bool: ...

class AspectRatioType(enum.Enum):
    """Aspect ratio types."""
    Pixel = 0
    """The value is the pixel aspect ratio, in place of the image's own."""

    Display = 1
    """The value is the aspect ratio of the whole picture."""

def getAspectRatioTypeEnums() -> list[AspectRatioType]:
    """Get every value of AspectRatioType."""

class AspectRatioOptions:
    """Aspect ratio options."""
    @overload
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, value: AspectRatio, type: AspectRatioType) -> None: ...

    @property
    def value(self) -> AspectRatio:
        """The aspect ratio. One that is not valid, as the default 0:0 is,
        leaves the image's own.
        """

    @value.setter
    def value(self, arg: AspectRatio, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def type(self) -> AspectRatioType:
        """Whether the value is a pixel or a picture aspect ratio."""

    @type.setter
    def type(self, arg: AspectRatioType, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: AspectRatioOptions, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: AspectRatioOptions, /) -> bool: ...

        """Set the list."""

        """Set the list only if it has changed."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear the list."""

    def setItem(self, index: int, value: DisplayOptions) -> None:
        """Set an item."""

    def setItemOnlyIfChanged(self, index: int, value: DisplayOptions) -> bool:
        """Set an item only if it has changed."""

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: DisplayOptions, /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

        """Insert an item."""

    def insertItems(self, index: int, list: Sequence[DisplayOptions]) -> None:
        """Insert a range of items."""

    def removeItem(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Remove an item."""

    def removeItems(self, start: int, end: int) -> None:
        """Remove a range of items."""

    def replaceItems(self, start: int, end: int, list: Sequence[DisplayOptions]) -> None:
        """Replace a range of items."""

    def get(self) -> list[DisplayOptions]:
        """Get the list."""

    def getSize(self) -> int:
        """Get the list size."""

    def isEmpty(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the list is empty."""

    def getItem(self, arg: int, /) -> DisplayOptions:
        """Get a list item."""

    def contains(self, arg: DisplayOptions, /) -> bool:
        """Does the list contain the given item?"""

    def indexOf(self, arg: DisplayOptions, /) -> int:
        """Get the index of the given item."""

    @property

    @cellCount.setter
    def cellCount(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.V2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def lineWidth(self) -> int:

class MissingIndicator:
    """Missing frame indicator.

    Marks a picture that stands in for a frame the media does not have, so a
    held or blank frame is not taken for the frame that was asked for.

    Drawn as a cross over the image. The other overlays -- the grid, the centre
    marker, the outline -- are aids for measuring a picture, and a mark that
    reads like one of them says the wrong thing about a frame that is not the
    frame asked for. A cross cannot be taken for a guide.

    It covers the part of the image that can be seen rather than the image
    itself, so zooming into the middle of the picture cannot hide it, the way
    it hides the outline.
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the indicator is drawn."""

    @enabled.setter
    def enabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def width(self) -> int:
        """The line width of the cross, in view pixels."""

    @width.setter
    def width(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def color(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F:
        """The cross color."""

    @color.setter
    def color(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: MissingIndicator, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: MissingIndicator, /) -> bool: ...

class ClippingWarningMode(enum.Enum):
    """What the clipping warning compares with its range."""
    AnyChannel = 0

    AllChannels = 1

    Luminance = 2

def getClippingWarningModeEnums() -> list[ClippingWarningMode]:
    """Get every value of ClippingWarningMode."""

class ClippingWarning:
    """Clipping warning: a pixel outside the range is covered with a warning
    color, red above and magenta below (the false color convention of the
    camera makers). The mode says what is outside: any channel, all three, or
    the luminance. The range is in displayed values, so the default marks what
    the display cannot show; 16/255 to 235/255 marks the video legal range.

    An overlay rather than a display adjustment so the picked color is the
    color under the warning, not the warning.
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the clipping warning is drawn."""

    @enabled.setter
    def enabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def mode(self) -> ClippingWarningMode:
        """What is compared with the range."""

    @mode.setter
    def mode(self, arg: ClippingWarningMode, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def low(self) -> float:
        """The bottom of the range; what is below it is marked magenta."""

    @low.setter
    def low(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def high(self) -> float:
        """The top of the range; what is above it is marked red."""

    @high.setter
    def high(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: ClippingWarning, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: ClippingWarning, /) -> bool: ...

class FrameGuide:
    """Frame guide: the frame of another aspect ratio within the picture, 2.39
    in a 16:9 picture say, outlined, with the rest masked. The lines are view
    pixels wide, so they stay one width however far the picture is zoomed. The
    aspect is kept as a ratio, so 16:9 is exactly that rather than 1.78.
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the frame guide is drawn."""

    @enabled.setter
    def enabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def aspect(self) -> AspectRatio:
        """The aspect ratio of the frame. One that is not valid draws no guide.
        """

    @aspect.setter
    def aspect(self, arg: AspectRatio, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def maskOpacity(self) -> float:
        """The opacity of the black mask outside the frame, from 0 to 1."""

    @maskOpacity.setter
    def maskOpacity(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def lineWidth(self) -> int:
        """The width of the frame's outline, in view pixels, inside the frame.
        """

    @lineWidth.setter
    def lineWidth(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def color(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F:
        """The outline color."""

    @color.setter
    def color(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: FrameGuide, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: FrameGuide, /) -> bool: ...

class SafeAreas:
    """Safe areas: the action and title safe areas, as fractions of the frame
    -- the frame guide's when it is on, the picture's otherwise.
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the safe areas are drawn."""

    @enabled.setter
    def enabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def action(self) -> float:
        """The action safe area, as a fraction of the frame's width and height.
        """

    @action.setter
    def action(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def title(self) -> float:
        """The title safe area, as a fraction of the frame's width and height.
        """

    @title.setter
    def title(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def lineWidth(self) -> int:
        """The line width, in view pixels."""

    @lineWidth.setter
    def lineWidth(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def color(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F:
        """The line color."""

    @color.setter
    def color(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: SafeAreas, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: SafeAreas, /) -> bool: ...

class DataWindow:
    """Data window: the outline of the pixels a file holds, which can be
    smaller than the picture, or reach outside it, as an OpenEXR data window
    can. Drawn for images whose tags give one (see tl::getDataWindow()). The
    lines are view pixels wide.
    """
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def enabled(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the data window is drawn."""

    @enabled.setter
    def enabled(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def lineWidth(self) -> int:
        """The line width, in view pixels, inside the data window's edge."""

    @lineWidth.setter
    def lineWidth(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def color(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F:
        """The line color."""

    @color.setter
    def color(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.Color4F, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: DataWindow, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: DataWindow, /) -> bool: ...

class ForegroundOptionsObserver:
    """Value observer."""
    def __init__(self, observable: IObservableForegroundOptions, callback: Callable[[ForegroundOptions], None], action: feather_tk._feather_tk.ObserverAction = feather_tk._feather_tk.ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class IObservableForegroundOptions:
    """Base class for observable values."""
    def get(self) -> ForegroundOptions:
        """Get the value."""

    def getObserversCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of observers."""

class ObservableForegroundOptions(IObservableForegroundOptions):
    """Observable value."""
    def __init__(self, arg: ForegroundOptions, /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: ForegroundOptions, /) -> None:
        """Set the value."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: ForegroundOptions, /) -> bool:
        """Set the value only if it has changed."""

    def get(self) -> ForegroundOptions:
        """Get the value."""

class TimeUnits(enum.Enum):
    """Time units."""
    Frames = 0

    Seconds = 1

    Timecode = 2

def getTimeUnitsEnums() -> list[TimeUnits]:
    """Get every value of TimeUnits."""

class TimeUnitsObserver:
    """Value observer."""
    def __init__(self, observable: IObservableTimeUnits, callback: Callable[[TimeUnits], None], action: feather_tk._feather_tk.ObserverAction = feather_tk._feather_tk.ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class IObservableTimeUnits:
    """Base class for observable values."""
    def get(self) -> TimeUnits:
        """Get the value."""

    def getObserversCount(self) -> int:
        """Get the number of observers."""

class ObservableTimeUnits(IObservableTimeUnits):
    """Observable value."""
    def __init__(self, arg: TimeUnits, /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: TimeUnits, /) -> None:
        """Set the value."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: TimeUnits, /) -> bool:
        """Set the value only if it has changed."""

    def get(self) -> TimeUnits:
        """Get the value."""

def timeToText(time: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime | None, units: TimeUnits, dropFrame: bool = False) -> str:
    """Convert a time value to text. An unset time gives the placeholder text
    for the units, so a widget with no value still reads as a time. Timecode is
    drop frame only when asked for: 29.97 is not drop frame unless the media
    says so.
    """

def isDropFrame(timecode: str) -> bool:
    """Get whether a timecode is drop frame, which the ';' before the frames
    says.
    """

class ITimeUnitsModel:
    """Base class for time units models."""
    def getLabel(self, time: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime | None) -> str:
        """Get a time label in the current time units. An unset time gives the
        placeholder text for the units.
        """

class TimeUnitsModel(ITimeUnitsModel):
    """Time units model."""
    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context) -> None:
        """Create a new model."""

    @property
    def timeUnits(self) -> TimeUnits:
        """Get the time units."""

    @timeUnits.setter
    def timeUnits(self, arg: TimeUnits, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def dropFrame(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether timecode is shown as drop frame."""

    @dropFrame.setter
    def dropFrame(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeTimeUnits(self) -> IObservableTimeUnits:
        """Observe the time units."""

class ImageSeqAudio(enum.Enum):
    """Image sequence audio options."""
    Ext = 1
    """Search for an audio file by extension"""

    FileName = 2
    """Use the given audio file name"""

def getImageSeqAudioEnums() -> list[ImageSeqAudio]:
    """Get every value of ImageSeqAudio."""

class Options:
    """Timeline options."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def imageSeqAudio(self) -> ImageSeqAudio:
        """Image sequence audio."""

    @imageSeqAudio.setter
    def imageSeqAudio(self, arg: ImageSeqAudio, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def imageSeqAudioExts(self) -> list[str]:
        """Image sequence audio extensions."""

    @imageSeqAudioExts.setter
    def imageSeqAudioExts(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def imageSeqAudioFileName(self) -> str:
        """Image sequence audio file name."""

    @imageSeqAudioFileName.setter
    def imageSeqAudioFileName(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def compat(self) -> bool:
        """Enable workarounds for timelines that may not conform exactly to
        specification.
        """

    @compat.setter
    def compat(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def threaded(self) -> bool:
        """Run the timeline on its own thread.

        When this is false the timeline has no thread and no read pool: a
        request is filled by the call that makes it, and the future it returns
        is already resolved. That is what a caller that only wants a frame or
        two wants, and it is what lets a thumbnail be taken without a thread
        per file.
        """

    @threaded.setter
    def threaded(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def readThreadCount(self) -> int:
        """How many sequence frames the timeline decodes at once.

        This is the one place the decoding concurrency is set. How many video
        requests are in flight follows from it, so that raising it is not
        silently undone by a separate limit.
        """

    @readThreadCount.setter
    def readThreadCount(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def audioRequestMax(self) -> int:
        """Maximum number of audio requests in flight.

        Unlike video, this does not follow readThreadCount: audio is not
        decoded by the timeline's pool. It comes from a reader that does its
        own threading, so there is no thread count here for it to follow and
        this is the only limit on how much audio is being assembled at once.
        """

    @audioRequestMax.setter
    def audioRequestMax(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def ioOptions(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        """I/O options."""

    @ioOptions.setter
    def ioOptions(self, arg: Mapping[str, str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def pathOptions(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.PathOptions:
        """Path options."""

    @pathOptions.setter
    def pathOptions(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.PathOptions, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: Options, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: Options, /) -> bool: ...

class System(feather_tk._feather_tk.ISystem):
    """Timeline system."""
    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context) -> None:
        """Create a new system."""

class Timeline:
    """
    A timeline opened for playback: an OpenTimelineIO file, a movie, an image sequence, or an opentimelineio Timeline object, with its media found and its video and audio described in ioInfo. Played by a Player.

    One frame of a sequence, such as render.0001.exr, opens that frame alone. For the whole sequence pass ftk.expandSeq(path, ftk.PathOptions()), which finds the frames beside it on disk.
    """

    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context, path: feather_tk._feather_tk.Path, options: Options = ...) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context, path: feather_tk._feather_tk.Path, audioPath: feather_tk._feather_tk.Path, options: Options = ...) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context, fileName: str, options: Options = ...) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context, fileName: str, audioFileName: str, options: Options = ...) -> None: ...

    @overload
    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context, otioTimeline: object, options: Options = ...) -> None:
        """
        From an opentimelineio Timeline object, without a file: a timeline built or edited in Python is played as it is. The object is copied, so later changes to it are not seen; make a new Timeline from it again.
        """

    @property
    def context(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Context:
        """Get the context."""

    @property
    def otioTimeline(self) -> object:
        """Get the OTIO timeline."""

    @property
    def path(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Path:
        """Get the file path."""

    @property
    def audioPath(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Path:
        """Get the audio file path."""

    @property
    def options(self) -> Options:
        """Get the timeline options."""

    @property
    def timeRange(self) -> opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange:
        """Get the time range."""

    @property
    def duration(self) -> opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime:
        """Get the duration."""

    @property
    def ioInfo(self) -> IOInfo:
        """Get the I/O information. This information is retrieved from the
        first clip in the timeline.

        The video information follows the media reference the clip is being
        read from, so that it describes the media on screen rather than the
        media that was active when the timeline was read.
        """

    def getMediaTime(self, time: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime) -> opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime | None:
        """The media time that names the frame shown at a timeline time.

        This is the time to show someone watching, whatever units they read it
        in: it matches the file on disk, where the timeline's own time only
        counts off the frames that are being played.
        """

    def getTimelineTime(self, time: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime, mediaTime: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime) -> opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime | None:
        """The timeline time that shows the given media time, taking the clip
        from the given time.
        """

    def getMediaFrame(self, time: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime) -> int | None:
        """The frame number the media gives to a timeline time."""

    def getMediaFrameTime(self, time: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime, frame: int) -> opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime | None:
        """The timeline time that reads the given media frame number, taking
        the clip from the given time.

        A frame the media does not have snaps as the media requires, so there
        is always an answer for a clip that was found.
        """

    def isMediaTimeContinuous(self) -> bool:
        """Whether media times increase over the whole timeline, which is what
        makes them worth showing in place of it.

        They do when every video clip reads the same media and takes a later
        part of it than the one before: one file played through, in one piece
        or in the runs a sparse sequence is cut into. Cutting between media, or
        playing the same media twice, restarts the numbering.
        """

    def getVideo(self, time: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime, options: Mapping[str, str] = {}) -> VideoFrame:
        """
        The video at a time, decoded: returns once it is, with no Player and no Context.tick(). For a script that wants frames rather than playback. Each call decodes its frame; nothing is read ahead or kept, as a Player does for playback. Frames for OffscreenRender.render() are a list of these, one per timeline. A time with no clip gives a frame with no layers, and a frame that cannot be read a layer whose image is None.
        """

class DetectCutsOptions:
    """
    Options for finding the cuts in a timeline. The defaults come from two films' edits checked against what was found.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def width(self) -> int:
        """The width frames are scored at."""

    @width.setter
    def width(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def threshold(self) -> float:
        """A cut is a frame scoring at least this, from 0 to 1."""

    @threshold.setter
    def threshold(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def blackThreshold(self) -> float:
        """
        The threshold after a black frame: a cut out of black scores lower than other cuts.
        """

    @blackThreshold.setter
    def blackThreshold(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def blackLevel(self) -> float:
        """A frame is black when its average luma is at most this."""

    @blackLevel.setter
    def blackLevel(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def relativeMin(self) -> float:
        """
        A frame under the threshold is still a cut when it scores at least this, and relativeRatio times the frames around it.
        """

    @relativeMin.setter
    def relativeMin(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def relativeRatio(self) -> float:
        """How far above the frames around it; zero turns it off."""

    @relativeRatio.setter
    def relativeRatio(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def relativeWindow(self) -> int:
        """How many frames on either side are around it."""

    @relativeWindow.setter
    def relativeWindow(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def minLength(self) -> int:
        """Cuts closer together than this many frames are one, the first of them."""

    @minLength.setter
    def minLength(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: DetectCutsOptions, /) -> bool: ...

class CutScore:
    """
    How different a frame is from the one before, from 0 to 1, as FFmpeg's scene filter scores it, and its average luma.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def score(self) -> float:
        """How different the frame is from the one before, from 0 to 1."""

    @score.setter
    def score(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def luma(self) -> float:
        """Average luma of the frame, from 0 to 1."""

    @luma.setter
    def luma(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: CutScore, /) -> bool: ...

def findCuts(scores: Sequence[CutScore], options: DetectCutsOptions = ...) -> list[int]:
    """
    The indexes of the frames that are cut to, from a list of scores; for trying other rules on scores already made.
    """

def scoreFrames(timeline: Timeline, range: opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange, options: DetectCutsOptions = ...) -> list[CutScore]:
    """
    Score each frame of a timeline over a range against the one before it. Reads every frame; give it a timeline of its own.
    """

def detectCuts(timeline: Timeline, range: opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange, options: DetectCutsOptions = ...) -> list[opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime]:
    """
    The times of the frames that are cut to, over a range: the cuts in an edit flattened to one movie or image sequence. Hard cuts only. Reads every frame; give it a timeline of its own.
    """

class PlayerCacheOptions:
    """Timeline player cache options."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def videoGB(self) -> float:
        """Video cache size in gigabytes."""

    @videoGB.setter
    def videoGB(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def audioGB(self) -> float:
        """Audio cache size in gigabytes."""

    @audioGB.setter
    def audioGB(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def readBehind(self) -> float:
        """Number of seconds to read behind the current frame."""

    @readBehind.setter
    def readBehind(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: PlayerCacheOptions, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: PlayerCacheOptions, /) -> bool: ...

class PlayerOptions:
    """Timeline player options."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def audioDevice(self) -> AudioDeviceID:
        """Audio device index."""

    @audioDevice.setter
    def audioDevice(self, arg: AudioDeviceID, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def cache(self) -> PlayerCacheOptions:
        """Cache options."""

    @cache.setter
    def cache(self, arg: PlayerCacheOptions, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def videoRequestMax(self) -> int:
        """How far ahead the player asks for frames while filling its cache.

        This is the player expressing demand, not a limit on how much is
        decoded at once; the timeline decides that. Keep it at or above the
        timeline's readThreadCount, or the decoding threads run out of work to
        do.
        """

    @videoRequestMax.setter
    def videoRequestMax(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def audioRequestMax(self) -> int:
        """How far ahead the player asks for audio while filling its cache.

        The player expressing demand, as with videoRequestMax above; the
        timeline decides how much of it is in flight.
        """

    @audioRequestMax.setter
    def audioRequestMax(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def audioBufferFrameCount(self) -> int:
        """Audio buffer frame count."""

    @audioBufferFrameCount.setter
    def audioBufferFrameCount(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def muteTimeout(self) -> datetime.timedelta:
        """Timeout for muting the audio when playback stutters."""

    @muteTimeout.setter
    def muteTimeout(self, arg: datetime.timedelta, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def sleepTimeout(self) -> datetime.timedelta:
        """Timeout to sleep each tick."""

    @sleepTimeout.setter
    def sleepTimeout(self, arg: datetime.timedelta, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def currentTime(self) -> opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime | None:
        """Current time to start at. Unset starts at the beginning."""

    @currentTime.setter
    def currentTime(self, arg: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime | None, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: PlayerOptions, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: PlayerOptions, /) -> bool: ...

    """Time actions."""
    Start = 0

    End = 1

    FramePrevious = 2

    JumpBack10s = 9

    JumpForward1s = 10

    JumpForward10s = 11

def getTimeActionEnums() -> list[TimeAction]:
    """Get every value of TimeAction."""

class TimelineListObserver:
    """List observer."""
    def __init__(self, observableList: IObservableTimelineList, callback: Callable[[Sequence[Timeline]], None], action: feather_tk._feather_tk.ObserverAction = feather_tk._feather_tk.ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class IObservableTimelineList:
    """Base class for observable lists."""
    pass

class ObservableTimelineList(IObservableTimelineList):
    """Observable list."""
    def __init__(self, arg: Sequence[Timeline], /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: Sequence[Timeline], /) -> None:
        """Set the list."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: Sequence[Timeline], /) -> bool:
        """Set the list only if it has changed."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear the list."""

    def setItem(self, index: int, value: Timeline) -> None:
        """Set an item."""

    def setItemOnlyIfChanged(self, index: int, value: Timeline) -> bool:
        """Set an item only if it has changed."""

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: Timeline, /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: Sequence[Timeline], /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    def insertItem(self, index: int, value: Timeline) -> None:
        """Insert an item."""

    def insertItems(self, index: int, list: Sequence[Timeline]) -> None:
        """Insert a range of items."""

    def removeItem(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Remove an item."""

    def removeItems(self, start: int, end: int) -> None:
        """Remove a range of items."""

    def replaceItems(self, start: int, end: int, list: Sequence[Timeline]) -> None:
        """Replace a range of items."""

    def get(self) -> list[Timeline]:
        """Get the list."""

    def getSize(self) -> int:
        """Get the list size."""

    def isEmpty(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the list is empty."""

    def getItem(self, arg: int, /) -> Timeline:
        """Get a list item."""

    def contains(self, arg: Timeline, /) -> bool:
        """Does the list contain the given item?"""

    def indexOf(self, arg: Timeline, /) -> int:
        """Get the index of the given item."""
