class Player:
    """
    Plays a timeline: decodes its video and audio, ahead of the current time, on threads of its own. What it has decoded reaches currentVideo and the observers only in Context.tick(), so a script calls tick() while it waits, sleeping a few milliseconds between calls: tick() does not wait for the threads. For frames without playback, Timeline.getVideo() needs neither.
    """

    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context, timeline: Timeline, options: PlayerOptions = ...) -> None: ...

    @property
    def context(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Context:
        """Get the context."""

    @property
    def timeline(self) -> Timeline:
        """Get the timeline."""

    @property
    def path(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Path:
        """Get the path."""

    @property
    def audioPath(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Path:
        """Get the audio path."""

    @property
    def playerOptions(self) -> PlayerOptions:
        """Get the timeline player options."""

    @property
    def options(self) -> Options:
        """Get the timeline options."""

    @property
    def timeRange(self) -> opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange:
        """Get the time range."""

    @property
    def duration(self) -> opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime:
        """Get the duration."""

    @property
    def ioInfo(self) -> IOInfo:
        """Get the I/O information. The information is retrieved from the first
        clip in the timeline.
        """

    @property
    def defaultSpeed(self) -> float:
        """Get the default playback speed."""

    @property
    def speed(self) -> float:
        """Get the playback speed."""

    @speed.setter
    def speed(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeSpeed(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableDouble:
        """Observe the playback speed."""

    @property
    def observeActualSpeed(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableDouble:
        """Observe the actual playback speed (speed * speed multiplier)."""

    @property
    def speedMult(self) -> float:
        """Get the playback speed multiplier."""

    @speedMult.setter
    def speedMult(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeSpeedMult(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableDouble:
        """Observe the playback speed multiplier."""

    @property
    def playback(self) -> Playback:
        """
        Stop, Forward or Reverse. Setting the direction it is already playing in doubles the speed, up to 64 times, as pressing play again does in a player; the other direction then halves it rather than turning round, and Stop returns it to normal. A script that only wants it playing checks playback first.
        """

    @playback.setter
    def playback(self, arg: Playback, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observePlayback(self) -> IObservablePlayback:
        """Observe the playback mode."""

    def togglePlayback(self) -> None:
        """Toggle the playback mode."""

    @property
    def isStopped(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether playback is stopped."""

    def stop(self) -> None:
        """Stop playback."""

    def forward(self) -> None:
        """Play forward: playback = Forward, speeding up when it already is."""

    def reverse(self) -> None:
        """Play in reverse: playback = Reverse, speeding up when it already is."""

    @property
    def droppedFrames(self) -> int:
        """
        The frames playback passed without presenting, because decoding or reading could not keep up. Counted only at normal speed or slower, and reset when playback starts or stops. Frames presented but never drawn are a viewer's to count; see Viewport.FPS.
        """

    @property
    def observeDroppedFrames(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableSizeT:
        """Observe the number of frames dropped during playback."""

    @property
    def loop(self) -> Loop:
        """Get the playback loop."""

    @loop.setter
    def loop(self, arg: Loop, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeLoop(self) -> IObservableLoop:
        """Observe the playback loop mode."""

    @property
    def playEveryFrame(self) -> bool:
        """
        Wait for each frame to be shown rather than pass frames the cache does not have yet, with the audio silent.
        """

    @playEveryFrame.setter
    def playEveryFrame(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observePlayEveryFrame(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableBool:
        """Observe whether every frame is played."""

    @property
    def currentTime(self) -> opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime:
        """
        The current time. Setting it seeks: the time changes at once, and the frame for it arrives in currentVideo once it is decoded.
        """

    @currentTime.setter
    def currentTime(self, arg: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeCurrentTime(self) -> IObservableRationalTime:
        """Observe the current time."""

    @property
    def observeSeek(self) -> IObservableRationalTime:
        """Observe seeking."""

    def timeAction(self, arg: TimeAction, /) -> None:
        """Time action."""

    def gotoStart(self) -> None:
        """Go to the start time."""

    def gotoEnd(self) -> None:
        """Go to the end time."""

    def framePrev(self) -> None:
        """Go to the previous frame."""

    def frameNext(self) -> None:
        """Go to the next frame."""

    @property
    def inOutRange(self) -> opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange:
        """Get the in/out points range."""

    @inOutRange.setter
    def inOutRange(self, arg: opentimelineio.opentime.TimeRange, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeInOutRange(self) -> IObservableTimeRange:
        """Observe the in/out points range."""

    def setInPoint(self) -> None:
        """Set the in point to the current time."""

    def resetInPoint(self) -> None:
        """Reset the in point"""

    def setOutPoint(self) -> None:
        """Set the out point to the current time."""

    def resetOutPoint(self) -> None:
        """Reset the out point"""

    @property
    def compare(self) -> list[Timeline]:
        """
        Timelines to compare with this one. currentVideo then has a frame for each, at the time compareTime says. How they are drawn together is CompareOptions, which the player does not use.
        """

    @compare.setter
    def compare(self, arg: Sequence[Timeline], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeCompare(self) -> IObservableTimelineList:
        """Observe the timelines for comparison."""

    @property
    def compareTime(self) -> CompareTime:
        """Get the comparison time mode."""

    @compareTime.setter
    def compareTime(self, arg: CompareTime, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeCompareTime(self) -> IObservableCompareTime:
        """Observe the comparison time mode."""

    @property
    def ioOptions(self) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Get the I/O options."""

    @ioOptions.setter
    def ioOptions(self, arg: Mapping[str, str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeIOOptions(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableStringMap:
        """Observe the I/O options."""

    @property
    def mediaReferenceKey(self) -> str:
        """Get the media reference key. An empty key, the default, leaves every
        clip on the media reference that OTIO has active.
        """

    @mediaReferenceKey.setter
    def mediaReferenceKey(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeMediaReferenceKey(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableString:
        """Observe the media reference key."""

    @property
    def mediaReferenceKeys(self) -> list[str]:
        """Get the media reference keys used by the timeline and any comparison
        timelines, sorted and without duplicates.
        """

    @property
    def compareMediaReferenceKeys(self) -> list[str]:
        """Get the comparison media reference keys."""

    @compareMediaReferenceKeys.setter
    def compareMediaReferenceKeys(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeCompareMediaReferenceKeys(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableStringList:
        """Observe the comparison media reference keys."""

    @property
    def videoLayer(self) -> int:
        """Get the video layer."""

    @videoLayer.setter
    def videoLayer(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeVideoLayer(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableInt:
        """Observer the video layer."""

    @property
    def compareVideoLayers(self) -> list[int]:
        """Get the comparison video layers."""

    @compareVideoLayers.setter
    def compareVideoLayers(self, arg: Sequence[int], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeCompareVideoLayers(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableIntList:
        """Observe the comparison video layers."""

    @property
    def currentVideo(self) -> list[VideoFrame]:
        """
        The video frames last decoded: one for this timeline, then one for each compare timeline. Updated only in Context.tick(), which does not wait for decoding, so it is empty until the first frame is in; sleep between ticks. No playback, clock or audio device is needed: a stopped player decodes the frame at its current time. After a seek it holds the previous frame until the new one is decoded, as a viewer keeps showing it, so check each frame's time against the time wanted rather than taking the first one that arrives.
        """

    @property
    def observeCurrentVideo(self) -> IObservableVideoFrameList:
        """Observe the current video frame."""

    @property
    def audioDevice(self) -> AudioDeviceID:
        """Get the audio device."""

    @audioDevice.setter
    def audioDevice(self, arg: AudioDeviceID, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeAudioDevice(self) -> IObservableAudioDeviceID:
        """Observe the audio devices."""

    @property
    def volume(self) -> float:
        """Get the volume."""

    @volume.setter
    def volume(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeVolume(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableFloat:
        """Observe the audio volume."""

    @property
    def mute(self) -> bool:
        """Get the audio mute."""

    @mute.setter
    def mute(self, arg: bool, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeMute(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableBool:
        """Observe the audio mute."""

    @property
    def channelMute(self) -> list[bool]:
        """Get the audio channels mute."""

    @channelMute.setter
    def channelMute(self, arg: Sequence[bool], /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeChannelMute(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableBoolList:
        """Observe the audio channels mute."""

    @property
    def audioOffset(self) -> float:
        """Get the audio sync offset (in seconds)."""

    @audioOffset.setter
    def audioOffset(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeAudioOffset(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.IObservableDouble:
        """Observe the audio sync offset (in seconds)."""

    @property
    def getCurrentAudio(self) -> list[AudioFrame]:
        """Get the current audio frames."""

    @property
    def observeCurrentAudio(self) -> IObservableAudioFrameList:
        """Observe the current audio frames."""

    @property
    def cacheOptions(self) -> PlayerCacheOptions:
        """Get the cache options."""

    @cacheOptions.setter
    def cacheOptions(self, arg: PlayerCacheOptions, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def observeCacheOptions(self) -> IObservablePlayerCacheOptions:
        """Observe the cache options."""

    @property
    def observeCacheInfo(self) -> IObservablePlayerCacheInfo:
        """Observe the cache information."""

    def clearCache(self) -> None:
        """Clear the cache."""

class Transition(enum.Enum):
    """Transitions."""
    Dissolve = 1

def getTransitionEnums() -> list[Transition]:
    """Get every value of Transition."""

def toTransition(arg: str, /) -> Transition:
    """Convert to a transition."""

def getExts(context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context, types: int = 7) -> list[str]:
    """Get the supported file extensions."""

class ExtGroup:
    """A named group of timeline file extensions, e.g. "Images"."""
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def label(self) -> str:
        """The name of the group, e.g. "Images"."""

    @label.setter
    def label(self, arg: str, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def exts(self) -> list[str]:
        """The file extensions, with the leading period."""

    @exts.setter
    def exts(self, arg: Sequence[str], /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: ExtGroup, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: ExtGroup, /) -> bool: ...

def getExtGroups(context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context) -> list[ExtGroup]:
    """Get named groups among the supported file extensions, for formats the
    plugin knows to belong together, e.g. "Camera Raw".
    """

def getPaths(context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context, path: feather_tk._feather_tk.Path, options: feather_tk._feather_tk.DirListOptions = ...) -> list[feather_tk._feather_tk.Path]:
    """Get a list of paths to open from the given path."""

class VideoLayer:
    """
    One track's image at a time: image, and imageB when a transition is blending into the next clip.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def image(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Image:
        """The image, or null when there is none. During a transition, the
        image of the clip going out.
        """

    @image.setter
    def image(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.Image, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def imageOptions(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.ImageOptions:
        """The options "image" is drawn with when the renderer is not given
        options of its own.
        """

    @imageOptions.setter
    def imageOptions(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.ImageOptions, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def imageB(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Image:
        """
        The image a transition blends into, by transitionValue: the clip after a dissolve. Empty otherwise -- a compared timeline is a VideoFrame of its own in Player.currentVideo, not an imageB.
        """

    @imageB.setter
    def imageB(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.Image, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def imageOptionsB(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.ImageOptions:
        """The options "imageB" is drawn with when the renderer is not given
        options of its own.
        """

    @imageOptionsB.setter
    def imageOptionsB(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.ImageOptions, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def transition(self) -> Transition:
        """The transition the layer is in at this time, or None."""

    @transition.setter
    def transition(self, arg: Transition, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def transitionValue(self) -> float:
        """How far through the transition the frame is, from zero at its start
        to one at its end.
        """

    @transitionValue.setter
    def transitionValue(self, arg: float, /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: VideoLayer, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: VideoLayer, /) -> bool: ...

class VideoFrame:
    """
    A timeline's video at a time: a layer for each enabled video track with a clip there, bottom track first. Player.currentVideo has one for each timeline, compared ones included.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None: ...

    @property
    def size(self) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Size2I:
        """The size of the timeline's video, from its I/O information
        (Timeline::getIOInfo()). The layer images may be other sizes.
        """

    @size.setter
    def size(self, arg: feather_tk._feather_tk.Size2I, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def time(self) -> opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime:
        """The time on the timeline the frame is for."""

    @time.setter
    def time(self, arg: opentimelineio.opentime.RationalTime, /) -> None: ...

    @property
    def layers(self) -> list[VideoLayer]:
        """The layers, one for each enabled video track with an item at the
        time, in track order.
        """

    @layers.setter
    def layers(self, arg: Sequence[VideoLayer], /) -> None: ...

    def __eq__(self, arg: VideoFrame, /) -> bool: ...

    def __ne__(self, arg: VideoFrame, /) -> bool: ...

class VideoFrameListObserver:
    """List observer."""
    def __init__(self, observableList: IObservableVideoFrameList, callback: Callable[[Sequence[VideoFrame]], None], action: feather_tk._feather_tk.ObserverAction = feather_tk._feather_tk.ObserverAction.Trigger) -> None: ...

class IObservableVideoFrameList:
    """Base class for observable lists."""
    pass

class ObservableVideoFrameList(IObservableVideoFrameList):
    """Observable list."""
    def __init__(self, arg: Sequence[VideoFrame], /) -> None: ...

    def setAlways(self, arg: Sequence[VideoFrame], /) -> None:
        """Set the list."""

    def setIfChanged(self, arg: Sequence[VideoFrame], /) -> bool:
        """Set the list only if it has changed."""

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Clear the list."""

    def setItem(self, index: int, value: VideoFrame) -> None:
        """Set an item."""

    def setItemOnlyIfChanged(self, index: int, value: VideoFrame) -> bool:
        """Set an item only if it has changed."""

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: VideoFrame, /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    @overload
    def pushBack(self, arg: Sequence[VideoFrame], /) -> None:
        """Append an item.

        Append a range of items.
        """

    def insertItem(self, index: int, value: VideoFrame) -> None:
        """Insert an item."""

    def insertItems(self, index: int, list: Sequence[VideoFrame]) -> None:
        """Insert a range of items."""

    def removeItem(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Remove an item."""

    def removeItems(self, start: int, end: int) -> None:
        """Remove a range of items."""

    def replaceItems(self, start: int, end: int, list: Sequence[VideoFrame]) -> None:
        """Replace a range of items."""

    def get(self) -> list[VideoFrame]:
        """Get the list."""

    def getSize(self) -> int:
        """Get the list size."""

    def isEmpty(self) -> bool:
        """Get whether the list is empty."""

    def getItem(self, arg: int, /) -> VideoFrame:
        """Get a list item."""

    def contains(self, arg: VideoFrame, /) -> bool:
        """Does the list contain the given item?"""

    def indexOf(self, arg: VideoFrame, /) -> int:
        """Get the index of the given item."""

class IRender(feather_tk._feather_tk.IRender):
    """
    The interface a timeline renderer implements, for the renderers made in C++ and the widgets that draw with them. To render frames from Python, use OffscreenRender, which needs no window.
    """

    def setOCIOOptions(self, arg: OCIOOptions, /) -> None:
        """Set the OpenColorIO options."""

    def setOCIOInputResolver(self, arg: Callable[[str, Mapping[str, str]], str], /) -> None:
        """Set a resolver for per layer OCIO input color spaces: given the path
        of the media a layer came from and the image's metadata tags, it names
        the input color space, or nothing. Layers whose own input is empty are
        resolved through it, so each clip of a timeline can be drawn through
        its own input. The results are cached per path until the options
        change.
        """

    def drawBackground(self, arg0: Sequence[feather_tk._feather_tk.Box2I], arg1: feather_tk._feather_tk.M44F, arg2: BackgroundOptions, arg3: CompareOptions, /) -> None:
        """Draw the background."""

    def drawForeground(self, arg0: Sequence[feather_tk._feather_tk.Box2I], arg1: feather_tk._feather_tk.M44F, arg2: ForegroundOptions, arg3: CompareOptions, /) -> None:
        """Draw the foreground."""

    def drawClippingWarning(self, arg0: int, arg1: feather_tk._feather_tk.Box2I, arg2: bool, arg3: Sequence[feather_tk._feather_tk.Box2I], arg4: feather_tk._feather_tk.M44F, arg5: ClippingWarning, /) -> None:
        """Draw the clipping warning over the rendered video, given as a
        texture drawn in the rectangle. Only the video boxes are covered; the
        empty part of the texture is not the video.
        """

class OffscreenRender:
    """
    Renders video frames to an image without a window: what a viewport would draw, a tile or wipe compare included, as an ftk.Image to write with WriteSystem or read with numpy.asarray(). The video alone is drawn, with no background or overlays; where no frame covers the image it is transparent. The OpenGL context is a hidden window's. On Linux with no display -- a container, a render farm, continuous integration -- set SDL_VIDEO_DRIVER=offscreen in the environment, which makes it an EGL context with no window system; that needs Mesa's EGL and DRI drivers, and uses the GPU where there is one and llvmpipe where there is not. Keep one and render the same frames again with other options -- a wipe position, a size, a look -- and the frames stay on the GPU instead of being copied in each time; see cacheByteCount and clearCache().
    """

    def __init__(self, context: feather_tk._feather_tk.Context) -> None:
        """Create a new renderer. Throws when there is no OpenGL context to be
        had.
        """

    def setOCIOOptions(self, options: OCIOOptions) -> None:
        """Set the OpenColorIO options."""

    def setLUTOptions(self, options: LUTOptions) -> None:
        """Set the LUT options."""

    @property
    def cacheByteCount(self) -> int:
        """
        The most bytes of frames kept as textures, so that rendering the same frames again -- with other compare options, another size or look -- does not copy them in again. Frames are told apart by the image, not its pixels. Zero keeps none, for frames each rendered once.
        """

    @cacheByteCount.setter
    def cacheByteCount(self, arg: int, /) -> None: ...

    def clearCache(self) -> None:
        """
        Clear the frames kept as textures: after changing an image's pixels in place, which otherwise renders as it was.
        """

    def render(self, videoFrames: Sequence[VideoFrame], compareOptions: CompareOptions = ..., size: feather_tk._feather_tk.Size2I = ..., imageOptions: Sequence[feather_tk._feather_tk.ImageOptions] = [], displayOptions: Sequence[DisplayOptions] = [], type: feather_tk._feather_tk.ImageType = feather_tk._feather_tk.ImageType.RGBA_U8) -> feather_tk._feather_tk.Image:
        """
        Render video frames -- the first and then one for each compared timeline, as Player.currentVideo has them -- laid out by compareOptions. The image is the size the comparison needs at the frames' own resolution, or the size given with the comparison fitted into it. type is what is read back: RGBA_U8 for a file or a look, RGBA_F32 to measure values past one where OpenGL can read it back -- OpenGL ES reads back bytes only, and a type that cannot be read back raises.
        """
